raw: 19.1 Soviet Active Measures: Definitions and Doctrine[^88][^89]
teaching_note: These U.S. historical assessments describe Soviet active measures from an institutional vantage point; distinguish their documented examples from their interpretations of intent and impact. A report about an adversary is not that adversary's own doctrine, and archive hosting does not make every assertion independently corroborated [@ageint088; @ageint089].
title: Soviet Active Measures: Definitions and Doctrine

raw: 19.2 Dezinformatsiya: Forgery, Front Organizations, Media Manipulation[^90][^91]
teaching_note: Forgery concerns authenticity; a false claim concerns content; intentional disinformation additionally requires evidence of knowing deception. The circulated State Department report in ageint090 is not independent corroboration of the same report elsewhere, while the 1986 speech in ageint091 is another source genre, not proof of every named campaign [@ageint090; @ageint091].
title: Dezinformatsiya: Forgery, Front Organizations, Media Manipulation

teaching_note: Keep organizational claims bounded by the report's date, author and evidence: a historical office or function does not establish a current roster or continuity of behavior. Distinguish formal responsibility, attributed conduct and demonstrated direction/control; do not identify present people or institutions from narrative similarity.
title: KGB Aktivnyye Meropriyatiya: Historical Organization

raw: 19.4 Historical Active Measures Campaigns: INFEKTION, RYAN, DENVER[^91]
teaching_note: The inherited list incorrectly groups warning intelligence with influence campaigns: the National Security Archive's inspected documentary briefing describes RYAN as an effort to detect a Western first strike, so consider it separately as a warning/confirmation-bias comparison, not an active-measures campaign (https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/briefing-book/aa83/2018-11-05/soviet-side-1983-war-scare). The cited speech does not establish the listed operations, nor does this source spine resolve whether INFEKTION and DENVER denote aliases or related components; hold those identities rather than count three independent cases. Any substantive history requires operation-specific archival support; the raw heading is retained as source identity, not endorsed as fact.
title: Historical campaign labels: attribution, warning and unresolved aliases

raw: 19.5 Russian Active Measures in the Contemporary Era[^92]
teaching_note: A literature review can support an attributed account within its period but cannot establish the sponsor of a newly encountered message. Distinguish observed dissemination, inferred coordination, inferred intent and audience effect; a capability or objective is not a measured outcome [@ageint092].
title: Russian Active Measures in the Contemporary Era

raw: 19.6 Chinese Information Operations: United Front Work Department
teaching_note: This named institutional topic remains a source gap: broad defensive guidance does not document the department's history, structure or responsibility for a particular activity. Do not collapse Chinese nationality, diaspora association, lawful advocacy and state direction into one category; a sponsor claim needs evidence of the actual relationship, not shared language or viewpoint.
title: Chinese Information Operations: United Front Work Department

teaching_note: The two links identify one NDU study by Fletcher Schoen and Christopher J. Lamb, not independent NDU and Brown findings. Its interpretation of the Active Measures Working Group is a retrospective case argument; distinguish the group's documented actions from causal claims about strategic effects and from general claims that exposure always works [@ageint093; @ageint094].
title: Deception, Disinformation, and Strategic Communications: NDU case study

raw: 19.8 AI-Driven Active Measures: Synthetic Influence at Scale[^95][^96]
teaching_note: Scale here means potential production or distribution volume, not geospatial resolution. Policy and position papers motivate research but do not show that more synthetic content produces greater persuasion, durable belief change or strategic success. Separate production capability, actual exposure, audience uptake and demonstrated effect; no detector score establishes an author or sponsor [@ageint095; @ageint096].
title: AI-Driven Active Measures: Synthetic Influence at Scale

teaching_note: Completed offline case: R1 is a synthetic rumor that a reading room has closed; R2 and R3 reproduce R1 verbatim; R4 is a dated service log showing one room closed for repairs; R5 records simultaneous repost times but no account-control evidence. The provenance result is one rumor origin, one independent service record and an ambiguous timing feature: complete closure is contradicted by R4, while coordination, intent and sponsor remain unknown. A withheld R6 shows R1 omitted the word 'upstairs'; revise the claim to a scope error, retain possible copying or scheduling as alternatives, and stop attribution rather than investigate accounts. Publish only a transparent factual correction in the exercise; confidence in a content finding never grants permission for public accusation or countermeasures (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]).
title: Countermeasures: Disinformation Detection and Response
